text.p: Former world champion Wendel Suckow of the United States grabbed his first World Cup victory this year in the final mens luge event of the season on Sunday at the Spiral bobsleigh and luge track.

Suckow, fourth after his first run, sailed down the serpentine course where luge events will be held at next years Nagano Olympics at the top speed of 127.6 kph to win with a time of one minute 41.667 seconds.
"Its been a slow year for me but it was picking up at the end," said Suckow, the 1993 world champion.
Suckow, 29, edged out Germanys Jens Mueller by 0.086 seconds while double Olympic gold medallist Georg Hackl, also of Germany, took the bronze in 1:41.813 under overcast skies.
Austrias Markus Prock placed fourth. Two weeks ago he secured his second straight World Cup overall title and the eighth of his career with a third-place finish in Winterberg, Germany.

"I had a very good season and Im now thinking about next years Nagano Olympics," said Prock, 32, who was runner-up at both the 1994 Lillehammer and 1992 Albertville Olympics. "The only thing lacking for me is an Olympic gold medal."
Prock won the overall title with a total of 230 points while Mueller took the silver with 182 points. Italys Wilfried Huber finished third on 169.
